title: Foodservice Plastic Smallware: How To Select Durable Dispensers and Portion Tools
summary: The best plastic foodservice smallware for a high-volume operation depends on the job, operating conditions and level of repeatability required.

Even simple tools can affect portion consistency, food handling, waste, service speed and quality across shifts or locations. Key selection factors include:


- Intended job

- Temperature exposure
- Impact and chemical resistance
- Cleanability
- Ergonomics and refill requirements
- Compatibility with the station, cabinet or existing workflow

## What Is Foodservice Plastic Smallware?


[Plastic foodservice smallware](https://www.sonoco.com/insights/foodservice-plastic-smallwares-guide-sonoco-products-company) refers to the smaller tools, containers and components used to prepare, portion, hold, handle or serve food in commercial operations. Reusable engineered plastic smallware includes commercial seasoning dispensers, foodservice portion control tools, food holding trays, pans and custom-molded components designed for high-volume environments. The broader category of restaurant smallwares can also include knives, utensils, cookware, plastic measurement tools, plastic portion cups and storage products.


## How To Choose Durable Plastic Foodservice Smallware


Buyers should assess smallware based on how it will be used in actual service rather than choosing by material or upfront price alone. The right durable plastic foodservice tools should meet the demands of the job, including exposure, cleaning, portioning and handling.


### Match the Material to Heat, Impact and Chemical Exposure


Engineered plastic smallware can meet demanding commercial environments when the material and product are designed and rated for the expected temperature, impact, chemical exposure and food-contact use.[Sonoco SonoWare](https://www.sonoco.com/sites/default/files/images/PDFs/Sonoco-Sonoware%20Updated%20Flyer-Proof.pdf) trays and pans are tested to withstand temperatures up to 375 degrees Fahrenheit, while Sonoco dispenser products are engineered for demanding foodservice environments.


Consider:


- Operating temperature
- Proximity to fryers, ovens or heated holding systems
- Frequency of drops and impacts
- Exposure to detergents and sanitizers
- Expected service life
- Manufacturer-stated use limitations


### Evaluate Cleanability and Sanitation Requirements


Reusable smallware must fit the operation’s actual cleaning process. A product that’s difficult to clean, disassemble or return to service can create unnecessary work between service periods.


Buyers should consider:


- How quickly the item can be cleaned between service periods
- Whether disassembly is required
- Areas where food or seasoning can accumulate
- Compatibility with the operation’s cleaning method
- Sanitation or cleanability certifications relevant to the application


### Determine How Much Portion Accuracy Matters


For operations trying to standardize seasoning or ingredient application, repeatable dispensing may matter more than overall dispenser capacity. Choosing the right foodservice portion control tools starts with understanding three distinct measures:


- **Capacity** : How much product the tool holds
- **Portion** : How much product the tool releases or measures during each use
- **Repeatability** : How consistently the tool reproduces that portion from one use to the next


Keeping these measures separate helps buyers choose for the required result rather than assuming greater capacity provides better portion control.


### Consider Ergonomics and Workflow Fit


Ergonomics and workflow fit determine how easily a dispenser or tray performs its intended task during service. Think about how the tool fits the people, space and sequence of steps involved in the job.


Consider questions such as:


- Can employees operate the tool quickly during peak periods?
- Can it be used with one hand where appropriate?
- How often must it be refilled or reloaded?
- Does it add unnecessary motions to the process?
- Does it fit the available station space?
- Can new employees understand how to use it with limited instruction?
- Does it integrate with existing holding or preparation equipment?

### Measured Salt Dispensers: Best For Repeatable Salt Application


A purpose-built measured plastic foodservice dispenser does more than store and distribute salt. Its operational value is repeatable dosing. Sonoco’s[AccuSalt dispenser](https://www.sonoco.com/sites/default/files/PDFs/AccuSalt_Short%20Product%20Flyer_FINAL.pdf) applies a consistent portion of salt to french fries and other fried foods and automatically recharges after use.


### Measured Seasoning Dispensers: Best For Consistent Seasoning Blends


Measured commercial seasoning dispensers reduce reliance on operator judgment by delivering a predefined quantity. Consistent portions help reduce food waste by limiting overapplication and unnecessary seasoning use while supporting consistent flavor across employees, shifts and locations. Sonoco’s AccuTaste® dispenser applies measured seasoning blends with fewer manual steps.


### Plastic Food Holding Trays and Pans: Best For High-Volume Holding Workflows


Rigid plastic food holding trays and pans can support high-volume food holding where temperature, cabinet fit, compartment design or food release are key considerations. Sonoco rigid smallware includes standard, custom and semi-custom configurations for different holding applications.


### Custom Molded Smallware: Best For Process-Specific Requirements


Custom or semi-custom smallware is appropriate when standard products can’t accommodate the needed geometry, equipment footprint or process. The next step is determining whether the application justifies custom development.


## Plastic vs. Metal Foodservice Holding Trays: What Should Buyers Compare?


Choosing between plastic and metal foodservice holding trays depends on the specific application, not the material alone. Buyers should compare product specifications against the food, holding temperature, cabinet, food-release requirements, handling frequency, cleaning process and tray configuration. Engineered plastic food holding trays can be a strong fit when food release, lighter handling or custom configurations are priorities. Metal tray performance depends on the material, construction and operating conditions.

Temperature Ratings vary by resin and product. SonoWare products are tested up to 190 degrees Celsius or 375 degrees Fahrenheit. Ratings vary by metal and tray construction. Verify the product’s temperature rating against the holding or cooking environment.

Custom configuration Injection molding can support custom shapes, compartments and features. Custom metal fabrication is possible through different manufacturing processes. Determine whether standard geometry meets the workflow before pursuing customization.

## When Does Custom Foodservice Smallware Make Sense?


Custom or semi-custom smallware is worth evaluating when an off-the-shelf product can’t adequately support the menu, equipment footprint, portion requirement or operating process.


### Signs an Off-the-Shelf Product May Not Be Enough


Explore custom development when a standard product creates a recurring mismatch between the tool and the job. Signs include:


- Employees rely heavily on judgment for a repetitive portioning task.
- Existing trays don’t match the holding equipment or menu format.
- A new menu item requires a different compartment or geometry.
- Smallware repeatedly creates sticking, handling or workflow problems.
- The operation needs to standardize the same process across multiple locations.
- Multiple tools could potentially be consolidated into a purpose-built component.

## What Information Should Buyers Define Before Contacting a Manufacturer?


Before contacting a manufacturer, define how the product will be used and the specifications needed to evaluate a standard product or begin discussing a custom solution.


Have these specifications ready:


- Application or food type
- Required portion or capacity
- Operating temperature range
- Food-contact requirements
- Cleaning method
- Required dimensions and cabinet or workstation constraints
- Handling requirements
- Expected frequency of use and service life
- Standard or custom requirements
- Anticipated production volume or rollout scale

## Frequently Asked Questions About Plastic Foodservice Smallware


### Are restaurant smallwares considered equipment?


Restaurant smallwares are generally considered tools and supplies rather than major foodservice equipment. Smallwares include items used for preparation, portioning, holding, handling and serving, while equipment typically refers to larger assets such as ovens, fryers, refrigerators and holding cabinets.


### What is the difference between a portion cup and a portion-control dispenser?


A plastic portion cup holds a predetermined amount of food, sauce or another ingredient. A portion-control dispenser measures or releases a defined quantity during use. The right choice depends on whether the operation needs to pre-portion a product or repeatedly dispense a consistent amount during preparation or service.


### What does NSF cleanability mean for foodservice smallware?


NSF cleanability requirements address whether a foodservice product is designed and constructed so it can be effectively cleaned and sanitized. Buyers should verify the specific NSF certification or standard that applies to the product and its intended foodservice use.


### How often should reusable plastic foodservice smallware be inspected?


Inspect reusable plastic foodservice smallware regularly based on frequency of use, cleaning practices and manufacturer guidance. Replace items when cracks, deformation, surface damage or other changes could affect safe use, cleanability or performance.
